text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Two policemen are abducted on their way to guard duty at the Indian High Commission, murdered and their bullet riddled bodies with their ears chopped off are dumped in Ngong forest.
- The only eight warehouses of Kenya"s giant supermarket chain Uchumi Supermarket, go up in flames.
- The search for more bodies from Wednesday"s Lake Victoria boat tragedy continues.
- A western Kenyan parliamentarian says Finance Minister Musalia Mudavadi is opposed by powerful figures in the ruling party.
- British fire experts fly in to help fight the fire raging on the Hong Kong cargo ship Oyster Bay at Mombasa port.
- Former opposition faction leader Raila Odinga says disgraced party officials plan to drag the ruling party into the controversial clearance of businessman Ketan Somaia.
- The Kalenjin and Kikuyu communities call for the revival of talks between the two to foster peace in the Rift Valley.

- The chief executive of a South African parks authority involved in a multi-billion dollar deal with Ketan Somaia"s Dolphin group says a senior government figure in Nairobi cleared Somaia of any wrongdoing in Kenya.
- Tanzania intends to limit the entry of expatriates for employment by foreign investors.
- The northern Ugandan rebel Lord"s Resistance Army spokesman was arrested in Nairobi last week as he was harming Kenyan relations with Uganda. ($1=54 Kenyan Shillings)
